# Miami Bee Rescue

> Miami-Dade County, Florida bee removal outfit that works only with live methods: wild honey bee colonies are boxed up and passed to beekeepers rather than killed.

Mobile crews only; there is no shop to visit. Crews travel to homes, condos, HOAs, businesses, docks, nurseries and farms anywhere in Miami-Dade County, and work nowhere outside it.

## Contact

- Phone and text: (786) 442-2496 (tel:+17864422496)
- Email: removal@miamibeerescue.com
- Service area: Miami-Dade County, Florida only
- Phones answered 24 hours a day, 7 days a week; response guaranteed within 24 hours

## What we offer

- Live, humane removal only; bees are relocated to beekeepers
- Licensed and insured; certificates of insurance for HOAs, condo associations and businesses
- Stinging emergencies handled first
- Thermal imaging used to locate hidden colonies
- Stucco, drywall, tile and paint put back by in-house licensed contractors, roofers and painters
- Warrantied workmanship: if bees return to a spot the company sealed, it comes back out
- Free quotes; night and weekend emergency calls cost more than weekday visits
- Typical ground-level jobs about $300 to $400; complex jobs with repairs can reach the thousands
- Photos of the work and an itemized invoice available on request

## Removal pages

- [24-Hour Emergency Bee Removal](https://miamibeerescue.com/removal/emergency/): Bees stinging, loose indoors or boiling out of a wall right now: what to do first and how a round-the-clock call works.
- [Swarm Pickup & Removal](https://miamibeerescue.com/removal/swarms/): Thousands of bees parked on a tree limb, side mirror or railing. How to tell a resting swarm from one moving in, plus live pickup and a ride to a beekeeper.
- [Bees in Block & Frame Walls](https://miamibeerescue.com/removal/walls/): Colonies inside concrete block cells or between wood studs, located with a thermal camera, taken out alive, and the opening closed and refinished by our own crews.
- [Tile & Flat Roof Hives](https://miamibeerescue.com/removal/roofs/): Colonies under barrel tile, flat tile and parapet roofs, located by thermal camera, taken out alive and closed up by our own licensed roofers.
- [Soffit, Fascia & Eave Hives](https://miamibeerescue.com/removal/soffits-eaves/): Bees living in a soffit, fascia gap or eave return: opened from below, colony taken out alive, cavity scraped clean and the roof edge closed again.
- [Meter, Valve & Irrigation Boxes](https://miamibeerescue.com/removal/utility-boxes/): Colonies in water meter boxes, sprinkler valve boxes, pool equipment pits and pull boxes, handled without tampering with anyone's equipment.
- [Palm & Tree Colonies](https://miamibeerescue.com/removal/trees-palms/): Colonies in palm boots and in hollow oak, mango and ficus trunks, taken out alive, with the cavity closed so the tree can keep standing.
- [Sheds, Garages & Outbuildings](https://miamibeerescue.com/removal/sheds-garages/): Colonies inside sheds, detached garages, workshops, outdoor kitchens and the cars, boats or furniture stored in them, opened carefully and moved alive.
- [Nurseries, Groves & Farms](https://miamibeerescue.com/removal/nurseries-groves/): Feral colonies in pump houses, shade houses, packing sheds and grove trees, moved out alive with field crews kept clear and pollination hives left alone.
- [Condo & High-Rise Buildings](https://miamibeerescue.com/removal/condos-high-rises/): Balcony planters, rooftop mechanical areas, garages and pool decks, handled with COIs, elevator bookings and the association kept in the loop.
- [HOA, Commercial & Property Managers](https://miamibeerescue.com/removal/hoa-commercial/): Removal for HOAs, property managers, restaurants, schools, warehouses and shops, with a COI before the visit and an itemized invoice for the file.
- [Docks, Seawalls & Boats](https://miamibeerescue.com/removal/waterfront-boats/): Colonies in boat covers, consoles, dock boxes, lift housings and seawall voids, taken out alive from waterfront homes and marinas across Miami-Dade.
- [Pool Enclosures & Equipment](https://miamibeerescue.com/removal/pool-enclosures/): Colonies in hollow screen enclosure beams, gutter ends, pump and filter covers, heater cabinets and pool cover reels, removed alive and sealed shut.
- [Live Honey Bee Removal](https://miamibeerescue.com/removal/live-honey-bees/): How a colony comes out alive: no spray, the comb located and cut out, and brood and bees boxed together for a beekeeper.
- [Humane Beehive Removal](https://miamibeerescue.com/removal/beehives/): For bees that have settled in and built comb: we open the space, move the colony alive, take out the wax and honey, and close it up.
- [Colony Relocation to Beekeepers](https://miamibeerescue.com/removal/relocation/): What happens to a colony after it leaves your walls: careful packing, an evening drive to a beekeeper and a new hive box, never a can of poison.
- [Comb & Honey Cleanup](https://miamibeerescue.com/removal/honeycomb-cleanup/): For the comb, honey and wax left after someone sprayed the bees or a colony moved out: cut out, cavity cleaned, entry sealed, surface repaired.
- [Repairs After Removal](https://miamibeerescue.com/removal/repairs/): The cut wall, lifted tile or open ceiling left by a hive, rebuilt and painted by in-house licensed trades instead of a second hired company.

## Place pages

- [Miami](https://miamibeerescue.com/miami-dade/miami/): The City of Miami proper, from frame houses on the river and MiMo hotels to Brickell towers, plus how to tell a city address from a county one.
- [Coral Gables](https://miamibeerescue.com/miami-dade/coral-gables/): Barrel tile, coral rock walls, 38,000 city trees and miles of waterway, with repairs planned around the city's tile and color approvals.
- [Coconut Grove](https://miamibeerescue.com/miami-dade/coconut-grove/): Hammock shade trees, coral rock walls and wood houses as old as the 1891 Barnacle: live removal in the Grove that leaves the canopy standing and matches the old materials.
- [South Miami](https://miamibeerescue.com/miami-dade/south-miami/): Old houses, deep shade and a Metrorail downtown. Live removal from South Miami walls, tile roofs, tree hollows and storefronts, with repairs by our own trades.
- [Westchester](https://miamibeerescue.com/miami-dade/westchester/): A mid-century house grid between Tamiami Trail and Bird Road, where seventy years of renovations leave gaps that bee colonies move into.
- [Miami Beach](https://miamibeerescue.com/miami-dade/miami-beach/): Barrier islands and bay islands: bees in Deco parapets, barrel tile, mansion soffits and condo tower roofs, with repairs matched to historic stucco.
- [Key Biscayne](https://miamibeerescue.com/miami-dade/key-biscayne/): Island village reached only by the Rickenbacker Causeway, with beach condominium towers, raised single-family houses and bayfront seawalls between two large parks.
- [Fisher Island](https://miamibeerescue.com/miami-dade/fisher-island/): A private island reached only by ferry or yacht. Live removal from tile roofs, palms and condo balconies, with crew clearance arranged before the crossing.
- [Bal Harbour](https://miamibeerescue.com/miami-dade/bal-harbour/): Ocean towers, a gated residential section and open-air shops at the island's tip, with utilities buried in ground-level boxes that bees like to claim.
- [Surfside](https://miamibeerescue.com/miami-dade/surfside/): A compact beach town where bees find gaps in mid-century block walls, flat roofs, condo mechanical spaces and front-yard meter boxes.
- [Bay Harbor Islands](https://miamibeerescue.com/miami-dade/bay-harbor-islands/): Two filled islands, apartments and shops on the east side and single-family homes on the west, linked to the mainland by the Shepard Broad Causeway.
- [Golden Beach](https://miamibeerescue.com/miami-dade/golden-beach/): A mile-long, single-family oceanfront town with one guarded entrance, tile roofs, docks and seawalls where honey bees move in quietly.
- [Miami Shores](https://miamibeerescue.com/miami-dade/miami-shores/): The 1920s 'America's Mediterranean' village of stucco, barrel tile and old shade trees, where colonies hide in historic walls and roofs.
- [Aventura](https://miamibeerescue.com/miami-dade/aventura/): Condo towers, a central golf course and water along the east; live removal with COIs and access plans for Aventura buildings and associations.
- [Sunny Isles Beach](https://miamibeerescue.com/miami-dade/sunny-isles-beach/): Barrier island towers, pool decks and garages, plus the older single-family houses of Golden Shores. COIs and board-ready photos included.
- [North Miami](https://miamibeerescue.com/miami-dade/north-miami/): A century-old bayfront city with postwar homes, canal lots and a guarded enclave, where loose soffits and block walls give colonies a way in.
- [North Miami Beach](https://miamibeerescue.com/miami-dade/north-miami-beach/): A mostly inland city on the coastal ridge, with mid-century block homes, enclosed carports, mobile homes and Eastern Shores condos around Maule Lake.
- [Miami Gardens](https://miamibeerescue.com/miami-dade/miami-gardens/): Mid-century houses on their own lots, where tired trim, vents, curbside meter boxes and back sheds give honey bees room to settle.
- [Hialeah](https://miamibeerescue.com/miami-dade/hialeah/): A crowded city of block walls, curb meter boxes and industrial yards, where one colony affects a whole street and sealing the opening matters.
- [Hialeah Gardens](https://miamibeerescue.com/miami-dade/hialeah-gardens/): One-story homes in the north, warehouse yards in the northwest and the Miami Canal to the southwest. Live removal with repairs and business paperwork handled.
- [Miami Lakes](https://miamibeerescue.com/miami-dade/miami-lakes/): A 1960s planned town of shade trees and 23 lakes, where hollow oaks and aging eaves give colonies room and guarded sections need entry planned.
- [Miami Springs](https://miamibeerescue.com/miami-dade/miami-springs/): Pueblo Revival flat roofs, parapets and stucco walls from the 1920s, a 1923 golf course and the airport along the south edge.
- [Doral](https://miamibeerescue.com/miami-dade/doral/): Warehouse parapets, dock canopies, townhouse soffits and golf course trees in a city where business parks sit next to family neighborhoods.
- [West Kendall](https://miamibeerescue.com/miami-dade/west-kendall/): Seven unincorporated communities on the county's southwest side, built around lakes and HOAs, where townhouse walls and block homes meet the farm fields.
- [Pinecrest](https://miamibeerescue.com/miami-dade/pinecrest/): Acre lots, specimen shade trees and 1950s ranch houses: where colonies hide in Pinecrest and how they come out alive.
- [Palmetto Bay](https://miamibeerescue.com/miami-dade/palmetto-bay/): Estate lots, Old Cutler Road and the Deering hammock next door: colonies here hide in sheds, trees, soffits and second-floor walls.
- [Kendall](https://miamibeerescue.com/miami-dade/kendall/): Unincorporated Kendall, from Dadeland west to the Turnpike: colonies in soffits, lawn boxes, old grove trees and plaza signage, removed alive and sealed.
- [Cutler Bay](https://miamibeerescue.com/miami-dade/cutler-bay/): A 2005 town over 1950s subdivisions and post-Andrew block homes, where colonies turn up in walls, tile roofs, valve boxes and lakeside eaves.
- [Homestead](https://miamibeerescue.com/miami-dade/homestead/): Rebuilt after Andrew and bordered by groves and nurseries, with colonies in soffits, block walls, meter boxes and farm sheds.
- [Florida City](https://miamibeerescue.com/miami-dade/florida-city/): The southernmost city in the county, where farmland meets homes and colonies move between fields, sheds and meter boxes.
- [Redland](https://miamibeerescue.com/miami-dade/redland/): Unincorporated farm country of groves, nurseries and five-acre lots, where wild colonies move into barns, pump houses, idle equipment and old fruit trees.

## Field guide

- [Scout bees around the house in Miami-Dade: what they are deciding](https://miamibeerescue.com/field-guide/scout-bees/): A few bees probing one crack in the house can mean a swarm is shopping for a home. How to read the signs and use the first two days.
- [Bees at a seasonal home in Miami while you are away](https://miamibeerescue.com/field-guide/second-home/): For owners who spend part of the year elsewhere: how bees move into a closed-up house, who notices first, and how removal works by phone and photo.
- [Bees in a Miami-Dade rental: who calls, who pays, who lets them in](https://miamibeerescue.com/field-guide/renters-and-landlords/): Tenant, landlord or condo association: what Florida's rental statute names, what your lease can change, and how to get bees out without a fight over the bill.
- [Bees found during a home inspection in Miami-Dade](https://miamibeerescue.com/field-guide/home-sale-inspection/): An inspector noted bees and the contract clock is running. What the termite report leaves out, what sellers owe buyers, and how to clear it before closing.
- [Bees after a hurricane in Miami-Dade: when the storm opens a hive](https://miamibeerescue.com/field-guide/after-a-storm/): What to do when wind damage leaves a live colony in the open: crews, chainsaws, debris piles and getting the bees out alive.
- [What a thermal camera shows about a bee hive in a Miami wall](https://miamibeerescue.com/field-guide/thermal-imaging/): How a thermal scan locates a colony by its nursery heat, why afternoon sun on stucco hides it, and what the screen will never tell you.
- [The Miami-Dade wall or box bees keep returning to](https://miamibeerescue.com/field-guide/why-bees-come-back/): Why a sealed-over or sprayed hive spot draws the next swarm, and what actually stops bees from moving back into the same wall or box.

Páginas escritas directamente para lectores hispanohablantes que buscan remoción de abejas en Miami-Dade.

- [Inicio](https://miamibeerescue.com/es/)
- [Precios](https://miamibeerescue.com/es/precios/)
- [Solicitar servicio](https://miamibeerescue.com/es/solicitar/)
- [Emergencias con abejas 24 horas](https://miamibeerescue.com/es/servicios/emergencias/): Picaduras, abejas dentro de un cuarto o una colonia junto al patio de los niños: qué hacer primero y cómo pedir ayuda a cualquier hora.
- [Enjambres de abejas](https://miamibeerescue.com/es/servicios/enjambres/): Racimos de abejas en ramas, cercas, balcones o carros: cuándo dejarlos ir y cuándo recogerlos vivos antes de que se metan en la casa.
- [Abejas dentro de paredes](https://miamibeerescue.com/es/servicios/abejas-en-paredes/): Abejas metidas en muros de bloque o de madera con estuco: localización con cámara térmica, remoción en vivo y reparación de estuco, drywall y pintura con equipos propios.
- [Abejas en techos y tejas](https://miamibeerescue.com/es/servicios/abejas-en-techos/): Teja de barril, teja plana y techos planos con parapeto: la colonia sale viva y nuestros propios techadores con licencia vuelven a colocar cada pieza.
- [Quitar panales y colmenas](https://miamibeerescue.com/es/servicios/panales-y-colmenas/): Colonias con panal dentro de paredes, techos o cajas: corte completo, abejas reubicadas vivas, cera y miel fuera, limpieza y sellado del hueco.
- [Remoción de abejas sin matarlas](https://miamibeerescue.com/es/servicios/remocion-sin-matarlas/): Abejas, reina y cría salen juntas en una caja de colmena rumbo a un apicultor. Sin insecticidas, con limpieza de la cera y la entrada sellada.
- [Abejas en el contador de agua](https://miamibeerescue.com/es/servicios/contador-de-agua/): Panal debajo de la tapa del contador, de la caja de riego o del foso de la piscina: cómo sacarlo vivo sin dañar el equipo ni la tubería.
- [Miami](https://miamibeerescue.com/es/zonas/miami/): Ciudad de Miami: casas de madera antiguas, torres y almacenes junto al río. Abejas fuera con vida, colonia localizada con cámara térmica y arreglos hechos por nuestra gente.
- [Hialeah](https://miamibeerescue.com/es/zonas/hialeah/): Hialeah: abejas en contadores de agua, muros de bloque calado y aleros de casas de posguerra. Remoción en vivo, reparación con contratistas propios y respuesta garantizada en 24 horas.
- [Hialeah Gardens](https://miamibeerescue.com/es/zonas/hialeah-gardens/): Hialeah Gardens: casas de un piso, almacenes del noroeste y la orilla del Canal de Miami. Las abejas salen vivas, la entrada se sella y la reparación la hacen contratistas propios.
- [Doral](https://miamibeerescue.com/es/zonas/doral/): Doral: almacenes, showrooms y urbanizaciones con asociación. Abejas vivas fuera de puertas enrollables, tejas y contadores de agua, con reparación de contratistas propios.
- [Kendall](https://miamibeerescue.com/es/zonas/kendall/): De Dadeland a Killian y Snapper Creek: colonias sacadas con vida de aleros, plafones y cajas de contador, y el hueco cerrado y reparado.
- [West Kendall](https://miamibeerescue.com/es/zonas/west-kendall/): Del Turnpike a Krome Avenue: paredes de concreto, townhouses de pared compartida y medidores en el césped. Colonias vivas ubicadas con cámara térmica y huecos que quedan reparados.
- [Westchester](https://miamibeerescue.com/es/zonas/westchester/): Westchester, entre Tamiami Trail y Bird Road: casas de posguerra con aleros y tejas que dejan pasar colonias, abejas reubicadas vivas y arreglos hechos por nuestra gente.
- [Homestead](https://miamibeerescue.com/es/zonas/homestead/): Homestead, entre los huertos de Redland y las casas reconstruidas tras Andrew: enjambres en frutales, colonias en muros de roca coralina, contadores de agua y aleros.
